starter_files.contents:
# Linux Disaster-Recovery Lab

Demonstrate safe recovery from planned failures in a disposable test environment.

## Required features
- [ ] Verified backups
- [ ] Recovery documentation
- [ ] Service restoration
- [ ] Verification and post-incident report

Use synthetic data and a disposable VM. Do not place passwords, private keys, or production data in this project. Document setup, tests, distribution/kernel assumptions, limitations, and recovery. State whether a check was run locally; CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary Linux/Bash commands inside the FastAPI web process.

stretch_features: Add automated tests over fixtures and boundary cases.
Add structured logs and machine-readable output.
Add a documented dry-run and rollback/recovery path.
Run static checks such as ShellCheck where applicable.

tests.name: Functional behavior
criteria: Required behavior works on synthetic inputs.
Expected output and exit status are documented.

tests.name: Safety and recovery
criteria: Dry-run or safe preview is available where state changes are possible.
A tested backup or rollback procedure is documented where relevant.

tests.name: Compatibility
criteria: Distribution and tool versions are identified.
Missing dependencies and unsupported cases have actionable messages.

review_method: Human review or execution in a separately isolated runner; the platform web process must not execute arbitrary Bash/Linux commands.
notes: Draft project based on Linux.pdf Section D. Relevant module numbers are 11, 16, 17, 18, 19, 24; require actual evidence of verification and recovery rather than claiming completion from a successful first run.
